Deterministically pick a representative value

Source: R/md-modal.R
md_modal_sql.Rd

Generates SQL that chooses, per group, the most frequently occurring value of a column, breaking ties by sorting the value itself. Used wherever an ingest collapses many source rows into one and has to keep a single spelling.

Usage

md_modal_sql(table, by, value, where = NULL, alias = NULL)

Arguments

table

Source table or CTE name.

by

Character vector of grouping columns.

value

Column whose representative value is wanted.

where

Optional SQL predicate applied before counting.

alias

Name for the generated CTE.

Value

A single SQL string defining the CTE.

Why not mode()

DuckDB's mode() returns an most-common value, not the most-common one. Under a tie it picks arbitrarily, and arbitrarily is not deterministically - the choice can differ between runs over byte-identical input.

That is not cosmetic. In the Schedule I ingest it changed the row count: a tie between '' and a real street name flipped which side of a non-empty filter the row landed on, and two consecutive runs produced address counts differing by one. Section 7c makes determinism a hard requirement - "the spec hash is worthless if the same spec can yield different rows" - so a build that cannot reproduce its own row count cannot be published against a hash at all.

The same objection applies to every "give me a representative" aggregate: mode(), any_value(), first(), arg_max() and arg_min() are all arbitrary under ties. None of them should appear in an ingest. This function exists so that the correct construction is shorter to write than the incorrect one.

What it generates

A row_number() window partitioned by the grouping columns and ordered by descending frequency then ascending value, filtered to rank 1. Frequency decides; the value's own sort order settles ties. Both halves are total orders over the input, so the result is a pure function of the data.

Alphabetical is an arbitrary tiebreak in the sense that no spelling is more correct than another - but it is a fixed arbitrary, which is the property that matters. Prefer it over anything data-dependent like "longest" or "most recent", which reintroduce ties of their own.

Examples

cat(md_modal_sql("si_clean", c("ein", "name_key"), "name_raw"))
#> modal_name_raw AS (
#>       SELECT ein, name_key, name_raw,
#>              row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY ein, name_key
#>                                 ORDER BY count(*) DESC, name_raw ASC) AS rk
#>       FROM si_clean
#>       GROUP BY ein, name_key, name_raw
#>     )
